case_title: State of Rajasthan v. Girdhari Lal
statutory_provisions: IPC s.304B (dowry death; charge framed under s.304B), with s.498A registered; on appeal, conviction altered to IPC s.306; Evidence Act ss.113A and 113B referred to
evidence_type: Medical (postmortem report and treating doctor's statement); ocular (oral witness testimony on cruelty and harassment); documentary
aggravating_circumstances: Alleged earlier attempt to burn the victim alive (as stated by PW.1); victim died within seven years of marriage by burn injuries
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC s.304B (dowry death); sentenced to life imprisonment
high_court_outcome: Appeal partly allowed; conviction altered from s.304B to s.306 IPC; sentence reduced to five years rigorous imprisonment and fine of Rs.1000 (default six months RI)
neutral_facts: The victim was married to the accused and died of burn injuries within seven years of the marriage. The victim's father filed a written complaint the day after the death, alleging that the accused and the accused's family had harassed the victim over dowry demands from the early days of the marriage. He also alleged that the in-laws had earlier tried to set the victim on fire and that neighbours had rescued her. The victim was admitted to hospital with burns all over the body and died during treatment the same afternoon. The postmortem examination recorded extensive burns as the cause of death. A witness stated that the accused used to beat the victim for dowry. The victim's father stated that the accused had beaten and harassed the victim for dowry after the marriage, and had earlier confined the victim in a room and tried to burn her alive by pouring kerosene; family members apologised and assured that it would not recur. The victim's mother testified that the couple visited her village about a month before the death and that the victim asked her to send her father because the accused harassed her. Other witnesses stated that the marriage took place about six or seven years earlier. A case was registered, investigated, and a charge sheet was filed.
physical_harm: Death by extensive burn injuries over the body
number_of_offences: 1 charged; 1 finally upheld (IPC s.306, as altered on appeal)
motive: alleged: cruelty and harassment connected with dowry demands by the in-laws; the Court did not find a specific dowry demand by the accused established
key_evidence_accepted: Postmortem report (Ext.P-6) and doctor's statement (PW.6) on burn death; ocular evidence of cruelty and harassment (PW.1, PW.7, PW.8); marriage date evidence (PW.2, PW.3) showing death within seven years; documentary evidence
witness_credibility: Court relied on ocular and documentary evidence showing cruelty and harassment, but found the dowry-demand statements of PW.1 and PW.7 non-specific as to the accused
custody_duration: More than six years undergone before the High Court judgment; High Court directed release if not required in other cases
trial_duration: offence: 10 August 1998; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 14 March 2007; Supreme Court: 7 October 2013
legal_representation: Accused: Satendar Sing Gulati, Kamaldeep Gulati. State: Archana Pathak Dave, Milind Kumar
investigation_status: FIR/complaint registered under s.304B and 498A IPC; investigation completed; chargesheet filed; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under s.304B, life imprisonment. High Court: partly allowed; converted to s.306, five years RI. Supreme Court: State's appeal dismissed
prosecution_argument: The victim died within seven years of marriage in unnatural circumstances; the accused did not inform the parents; PW.1, PW.4 and PW.7 spoke of dowry-related harassment corroborated by other witnesses and documents; High Court erred in converting to s.306 and reducing sentence
defence_argument: Supported the High Court's decision converting the conviction to s.306 and reducing the sentence
legal_principle_applied: s.304B requires cruelty or harassment soon before death connected with dowry demand; s.113B presumption not available without that ingredient; s.113A presumption of abetment of suicide within seven years of marriage applies where cruelty is established
sentencing_rationale: Not applicable (no fresh sentence imposed; Supreme Court declined to interfere with High Court's sentence)
